context.analysis:
## Overview
The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe with a modern Azure platform via a hybrid architecture. It enables online claims submission and adjuster workflows while ensuring continuous legacy operation and strict data consistency.

## Key Elements
* Customer / Broker: External actors submitting claims online.
* Claims Adjuster: Internal users handling claims via the new web application.
* Legacy Mainframe: On-premises COBOL/DB2 system of record.
* Modern Claims Platform: Azure-hosted system featuring the Core Insurance Datastore.
* Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL): Isolation layer mitigating mainframe schema volatility.
* Identity Provider: Insurer Active Directory / Azure AD.

## Relationships
* Customer/Broker to Modern Claims Platform: HTTPS/REST for claim submission.
* Claims Adjuster to Modern Claims Platform: HTTPS for web application access under 2s.
* Modern Claims Platform to Anti-Corruption Layer: Internal REST/Messaging.
* Anti-Corruption Layer to Legacy Mainframe: HTTPS/REST and MQ for asynchronous state synchronization.
* Modern Claims Platform to Identity Provider: OpenID Connect / SAML for Single Sign-On.

## Technology Stack
* Azure Cloud (PaaS/Serverless): Mitigates team's cloud inexperience and accelerates delivery.
* Azure SQL / Cosmos DB: Core Insurance Datastore ensuring eventual consistency for claims.
* Azure Service Bus: Asynchronous messaging to isolate mainframe latency and batch windows.
* IBM z/OS & DB2: Legacy system of record maintained on-premises.

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates mainframe volatility through an Anti-Corruption Layer and asynchronous messaging, protecting strict batch constraints and latency requirements. It enables incremental claim-type migration while maintaining operational continuity and security over a 3-year timeline.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a legacy COBOL/DB2 mainframe with a hybrid cloud platform. It enables online claims submission and adjuster workflows while maintaining synchronization with the legacy system of record.

## Key Elements
* Customer Portal (Azure Static Web Apps / React)
* Adjuster Workspace (Azure Container Apps / .NET Core)
* API Gateway (Azure Container Apps / .NET Yit)
* Claims Core Service (Azure Container Apps / .NET Core)
* Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) (Azure Container Apps / Camel or .NET)
* Integration Message Broker (Azure Service Bus)
* Database (Azure SQL Database / EF Core)
* Legacy Mainframe (COBOL/DB2 on-premise)
* Identity Provider (Microsoft Entra ID / OpenID Connect)

## Relationships
* Customer Portal & Adjuster Workspace $\rightarrow$ API Gateway via HTTPS/WSS
* API Gateway $\rightarrow$ Claims Core Service & Adjuster Workspace via gRPC/HTTP
* API Gateway $\leftrightarrow$ Identity Provider via OpenID Connect
* Claims Core Service $\leftrightarrow$ Integration Message Broker via AMQP
* Integration Message Broker $\rightarrow$ ACL via AMQP
* ACL $\rightarrow$ Legacy Mainframe via MQ/File Transfer

## Technology Stack
* Azure West Europe: Primary cloud region chosen for the modern platform containers.
* .NET Core / C#: Core application runtime chosen to balance enterprise standards with team capabilities.
* Azure Container Apps: Container hosting platform to simplify cloud deployment for an inexperienced team.
* Azure Service Bus: Message broker ensuring reliable at-least-once message delivery.
* Azure SQL Database / EF Core: Relational storage supporting the CQRS read models.
* Microsoft Entra ID: Single sign-on integration with on-premise Active Directory.

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates the expensive-to-change legacy mainframe behind an Anti-Corruption Layer while using asynchronous messaging to guarantee consistency and sub-second performance. The chosen Azure and .NET technologies lower the adoption barrier for a team with limited cloud experience.

Customer Portal.analysis:
## Overview
The Customer Portal is a React-based single-page application hosted on Azure Static Web Apps enabling secure online claim submissions for customers and brokers. It acts as the front-end entry point within a hybrid cloud modernization architecture for the insurance claims platform.

## Key Elements
* Customer / Broker (Person)
* Customer Portal Container (Azure Static Web Apps / React SPA)
* Authentication Controller (TypeScript / MSAL.js Component)
* Claim Submission UI (React / Formik Component)
* Claim Tracker Component (React Component)
* API Client Service (Axios / OpenAPI Generated Component)
* API Gateway (Azure Container Apps / .NET Yarp)
* Identity Provider (Active Directory)

## Relationships
* Customer / Broker -> Customer Portal: Submits claims online [HTTPS]
* Authentication Controller -> Identity Provider: Authenticates via Single Sign-On [OIDC/HTTPS]
* Claim Submission UI -> API Client Service: Delegates payload validation and invocation [TypeScript Function Call]
* API Client Service -> API Gateway: Sends API requests and receives real-time updates [HTTPS/JSON, WSS]

## Technology Stack
* Azure Static Web Apps: Hosts the React application with minimal operational overhead for cloud-inexperienced teams
* React & Formik: Powers dynamic, type-specific claim forms with fast client-side rendering
* MSAL.js & OIDC: Implements secure Single Sign-On integration with Active Directory
* TypeScript & OpenAPI: Ensures end-to-end type safety between the SPA and API Gateway via auto-generated clients
* Axios & WebSockets (WSS): Handles asynchronous command execution and real-time claim status tracking

## Rationale
This architecture minimizes operational complexity for a cloud-inexperienced team by utilizing serverless static hosting and client-side rendering. It strictly satisfies security and performance requirements through integrated Azure Active Directory authentication and direct API Gateway communication.

Adjuster Workspace.analysis:
## Overview
The Adjuster Workspace is a .NET Core Backend-for-Frontend and React application that enables claims adjusters to process claims efficiently. It isolates the user interface from high-latency backend systems to meet strict performance requirements.

## Key Elements
- UI Shell (React SPA)
- BFF API Controller (.NET Core)
- Event-Driven Sync Worker (.NET Core Background Service)
- Async View Model Cache (Azure Cache for Redis)
- ACL Integration Client (.NET Core / gRPC)

## Relationships
- UI Shell -> BFF API Controller: API requests [HTTPS/REST]
- BFF API Controller -> Async View Model Cache: Read/Write pre-aggregated claim states [TCP]
- BFF API Controller -> API Gateway: Outbound commands [gRPC/HTTPS]
- Integration Message Broker -> Event-Driven Sync Worker: Consume claim events [AMQP]
- Event-Driven Sync Worker -> Async View Model Cache: Update cached view models [TCP]

## Technology Stack
- UI Shell: React SPA for modern client-side rendering
- BFF API Controller & Sync Worker: .NET Core for robust enterprise backend logic
- Async View Model Cache: Azure Cache for Redis for sub-millisecond read performance
- Integration Protocol: gRPC and HTTPS for secure inter-service communication

## Rationale
This component architecture uses a Backend-for-Frontend pattern combined with a Redis cache to decouple synchronous UI reads from slow downstream systems. This guarantees sub-2-second screen loads for adjusters, satisfying strict performance SLAs despite high legacy mainframe latency.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims system with a modern hybrid cloud platform. It enables online claim submission, adjuster workflows, and incremental claim type migration while maintaining data consistency.

## Key Elements
* Customer / Broker
* Claims Adjuster
* Legacy Mainframe (COBOL/DB2)
* Identity Provider (Azure Active Directory)
* Customer Portal (Azure Static Web Apps / React)
* Adjuster Workspace (Azure Container Apps / .NET Core)
* API Gateway (Azure Container Apps / .NET YARP)
* Claims Core Service (Azure Container Apps / .NET Core)
* Integration Message Broker (Azure Service Bus)
* Database (Azure SQL Database / EF Core)
* Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL)
* API Gateway Components: Routing Engine, Authentication & Authorization Filter, Rate Limiting & Resiliency Policy Middleware, Transformation & Protocol Bridge

## Relationships
* Customer Portal -> API Gateway: API requests [HTTPS/WSS]
* Adjuster Workspace -> API Gateway: API requests [HTTPS/WSS]
* API Gateway -> Claims Core Service: Routes claims requests [gRPC/HTTP]
* API Gateway -> Identity Provider: Authenticates users [OpenID Connect]
* Customer Portal -> Authentication & Authorization Filter: Validates tokens [HTTPS]
* Routing Engine -> Transformation & Protocol Bridge: Passes raw requests [In-memory]
* Transformation & Protocol Bridge -> Claims Core Service: Forwards gRPC commands [gRPC/HTTP2]

## Technology Stack
* Azure Container Apps: Hosting containerized microservices to accommodate team's limited cloud experience.
* .NET YARP (Yet Another Reverse Proxy): High-performance routing integrated natively with .NET.
* gRPC/HTTP2: Inter-service communication for low latency and efficient serialization.
* Azure Active Directory / OpenID Connect: Secure single sign-on satisfying security requirements.
* Polly (.NET): Transient fault handling and circuit breakers for slow mainframe responses.

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates expensive mainframe changes behind an Anti-Corruption Layer while enabling incremental migration of claim types. The cloud-native Azure and .NET stack balances modern performance needs with the team's existing skill set.

Claims Core Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Claims Core Service container uses a modular .NET Core component architecture deployed in Azure Container Apps to gradually migrate claim types from a legacy mainframe. It ensures high performance, transactional consistency, and rapid rollback capabilities during the hybrid cloud transition.

## Key Elements
- Claim Submission Controller (.NET Core API)
- Claims Router / Strategy Selector (.NET Core)
- Claim Workflow Engine (.NET Core / Workflow Core)
- Data Access Repository (Entity Framework Core)
- Mainframe Sync Publisher (.NET Core)
- Outbox Processor (.NET Core Background Service)
- Mainframe Anti-Corruption Client (.NET Core)

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> Claim Submission Controller: Routes incoming requests [gRPC]
- Claim Submission Controller -> Claims Router / Strategy Selector: Forwards requests for evaluation [In-Memory]
- Claims Router / Strategy Selector -> Claim Workflow Engine: Executes modern claim workflows [In-Memory]
- Claims Router / Strategy Selector -> Mainframe Anti-Corruption Client: Forwards unmigrated claims [HTTP/AMQP]
- Claim Workflow Engine -> Data Access Repository: Persists state and domain models [EF Core / TDS]
- Data Access Repository -> Outbox Processor: Stores transactional outbox events [EF Core / TDS]
- Outbox Processor -> Integration Message Broker: Publishes reliable domain events [AMQP]
- Mainframe Sync Publisher -> Integration Message Broker: Synchronizes state with legacy system [AMQP]

## Technology Stack
- .NET Core: Selected for core components due to team familiarity and strong enterprise ecosystem
- Entity Framework Core / TDS: Manages relational persistence with Azure SQL Database ensuring ACID compliance
- Workflow Core: Manages complex state transitions for migrated claim types
- Azure Service Bus: Handles asynchronous messaging via AMQP for decoupling and event distribution
- Transactional Outbox Pattern: Prevents dual-write consistency issues between the database and message broker

## Rationale
This component architecture isolates complex routing and state management, allowing individual claim types to be migrated or rolled back within one day. Furthermore, the outbox pattern and anti-corruption client decouple the modern UI from slow mainframe responses, satisfying strict performance and consistency constraints.

level: component
scope: "Component diagram for the Claims Core Service container"
parentContainer:

elements:
  - type: "component"
    name: "Claim Submission Controller"
    technology: ".NET Core API"
    description: "Handles incoming claim submission requests."
  - type: "component"
    name: "Claims Router / Strategy Selector"
    technology: ".NET Core"
    description: "Evaluates and routes claims to either modern workflows or the mainframe."
  - type: "component"
    name: "Claim Workflow Engine"
    technology: ".NET Core / Workflow Core"
    description: "Executes modern claim workflows and manages complex state transitions."
  - type: "component"
    name: "Data Access Repository"
    technology: "Entity Framework Core"
    description: "Persists state and domain models using Azure SQL Database."
  - type: "component"
    name: "Mainframe Sync Publisher"
    technology: ".NET Core"
    description: "Synchronizes state with the legacy mainframe system."

Integration Message Broker.analysis:
## Overview
The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe with a modern hybrid cloud platform. It enables online claims submission and adjuster workflows while maintaining synchronization with the legacy system of record.

## Key Elements
- Customer / Broker (Person)
- Claims Adjuster (Person)
- Customer Portal (Azure Static Web Apps / React)
- Adjuster Workspace (Azure Container Apps / .NET Core)
- API Gateway (Azure Container Apps / .NET Yit)
- Claims Core Service (Azure Container Apps / .NET Core)
- Integration Message Broker (Azure Service Bus with Claim Routing Topic, Session Processor, and Dead-Letter Subsystem)
- Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) (On-premise / Azure)
- Database (Azure SQL Database / EF Core)
- Legacy Mainframe (On-prem-mainframe / COBOL/DB2)
- Identity Provider (Azure Active Directory)

## Relationships
- Customer / Broker -> Customer Portal: Submits claims [HTTPS]
- Claims Adjuster -> Adjuster Workspace: Manages claims [HTTPS/SSO]
- Customer Portal -> API Gateway: Forwards online claims [HTTPS/REST]
- Adjuster Workspace -> API Gateway: Executes adjuster operations [HTTPS/REST]
- API Gateway -> Claims Core Service: Routes API requests [gRPC/Internal]
- Claims Core Service -> Database: Reads/writes claim state [ADO.NET/EF Core]
- Claims Core Service -> Claim Routing Topic: Publishes domain events [AMQP over TLS]
- Claim Routing Topic -> Session Processor: Enforces ordered delivery per session ID [AMQP]
- Session Processor -> Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL): Forwards synchronized events [AMQP]
- ACL -> Legacy Mainframe: Synchronizes claim data [Batch/Interface]

## Technology Stack
- Azure Service Bus: Chosen for native persistent messaging, duplicate detection, and dead-lettering to satisfy zero-data-loss requirements (R-04).
- Azure Container Apps & .NET Core: Provides scalable, maintainable microservices with low cloud-experience overhead.
- Azure SQL Database with EF Core: Delivers reliable relational persistence for the modern platform.
- Azure Active Directory: Enables seamless Single Sign-On (R-07) across internal user workspaces.

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates expensive mainframe changes while allowing incremental claim-type migration via Azure Service Bus routing and sessions. It decouples the sub-second modern UI from slower legacy responses, ensuring high performance and maintainability.

Database.analysis:
## Overview
The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe with a modern Azure-hosted hybrid platform. It ensures seamless claim processing, zero data loss, and sub-second adjuster UI response times during the multi-year migration.

## Key Elements
* Customer / Broker & Claims Adjuster (Users)
* Legacy Mainframe & Active Directory (External Systems)
* Customer Portal (Azure Static Web Apps / React)
* Adjuster Workspace (Azure Container Apps / .NET Core)
* API Gateway (Azure Container Apps / .NET Yit)
* Claims Core Service (Azure Container Apps / .NET Core)
* Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL)
* Integration Message Broker (Azure Service Bus)
* Database (Azure SQL Database / EF Core) containing:
  - Claim Write Model Component
  - Claim Read Model Component
  - Migration & Audit Log Component
  - Integration Staging Component

## Relationships
* Customer / Broker -> Customer Portal: Submits online claims [HTTPS / TLS]
* Claims Adjuster -> Adjuster Workspace: Manages claims [HTTPS / TLS]
* Customer Portal & Adjuster Workspace -> API Gateway: Routes requests [HTTPS / REST]
* API Gateway -> Claims Core Service: Dispatches business logic [gRPC / Internal Network]
* Claims Core Service -> Database: Reads/writes domain data [EF Core / TDS]
* Claims Core Service -> Integration Staging Component: Transforms staged payloads [Stored Procedures / TDS]
* Claims Core Service <-> Integration Message Broker: Publishes/consumes events [AMQP / Azure Service Bus]
* Anti-Corruption Layer <-> Legacy Mainframe: Syncs claim types [MQ / SNA]
* Adjuster Workspace -> Active Directory: Authenticates users [OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0]

## Technology Stack
* Azure West Europe & On-Premises Mainframe: Hybrid cloud foundation meeting data residency and connectivity needs.
* Azure Container Apps & .NET Core: Scalable microservices architecture for APIs and workers.
* Azure SQL Database & EF Core: Relational storage using Temporal Tables, Row-Level Security, and JSON Support for CQRS, auditability, and rapid staging.
* Azure Service Bus: Asynchronous messaging guaranteeing reliable event-driven state synchronization.
* Azure Static Web Apps & React: High-performance frontend for customer interactions.

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates expensive mainframe changes behind an Anti-Corruption Layer while modernizing the user experience in Azure. It leverages CQRS and database staging components to meet strict consistency, performance, and one-day rollback requirements.
